text:
elaine_pm: Hey team — starting a PRD intake for a compliance-driven feature: revocable/auditable response snapshots. Problem: some regulated customers need an append-only, auditable view of model outputs tied to a revocation action (e.g., delete or redact a specific user output) and a clear audit trail for requests that were served. We need proposal + acceptance criteria.

mike_sre: 👍 need to understand perf and storage impact. will this be enabled per-tenant or per-route?

elaine_pm: Per-tenant opt-in to start. Also a per-route flag for fine-grained control. Goals: 1) create immutable snapshot record for each accepted response (schema below) 2) provide an API to request revocation/redaction with audit entry 3) ensure snapshots are queryable for standard audit windows (90/180/360 days) 4) minimal perf penalty on p95 latency (<5% overhead).

sam_research: Important to capture enough context to replay/debug. Propose snapshot fields: request_id, model_id, model_version, prompt_hash, token_count, deterministic_seed (if available), response_blob (encrypted), snapshot_ts, tenant_id, route, revocation_status. Example schema: ```json
{"request_id":"req_XXX","tenant_id":"t_123","model":"redwood-3b","response_blob":"<enc>","snapshot_ts":1670000000}"```

jordan_eng: Edge cases: streaming responses (partial snapshots?), high-QPS tenants (sampling vs full capture), and KV cache sensitive data. Also how do we handle function-calls that include PII in arguments?

olivia_legal: From compliance side: we need immutable audit records but also the *ability* to remove PII on customer request. So revocation must be supported (mark redacted + create redaction-proof audit entry). Also chain-of-custody: who requested revocation and why.

elaine_pm: Non-goals: full-text search across snapshot blobs in phase-1, and long-term archival beyond configured retention. We'll do sampled export hooks for analytics later.

mike_sre: Ops constraints: storage options: encrypted object store with per-tenant KMS keys, or short-lived cache + export. Cost tradeoffs: storing every token will be expensive. Suggest default to 1) store metadata for all requests, 2) store full encrypted blob only for requests that hit a configurable size threshold or are flagged by a sampling rule.

sam_research: Acceptance criteria (PRD):
- Config flag: tenant.opt_in_revocable_snapshots (boolean) and route-level overrides.
- Snapshot API returns snapshot_id immediately after response is accepted.
- Revocation API: POST /revocations {snapshot_id, reason} -> creates immutable revocation record; snapshot_blob replaced with redaction token while preserving metadata.
- Audit query API: GET /snapshots?tenant_id=..&from=..&to=.. returns matches and revocation_status.
- Performance: enabling full snapshots for a test tenant should not increase median latency by >2% and p95 by <5%.

jordan_eng: Implementation notes: integrate at response-commit point to avoid capturing intermediate generations. For streaming, capture final assembled output at commit; for multimodal/function-calls, capture both response and function args (encrypted). Need backward-compatible schema versioning.

olivia_legal: Also require an immutable revocation log entry that includes actor (user/service), timestamp, and reason. Redaction should be reversible only by reprocessing (i.e., we don't keep plaintext after redaction).

elaine_pm: Success metrics for alpha:
- 3 pilot customers onboarded and performing audits at least once per month.
- Audit query latency < 200ms for common queries.
- No compliance incidents from revocation process in first 6 months.
- Cost overhead < 10% on tenant bill for pilot (with sampling defaults).

mike_sre: Questions: retention slider UX in Console? KMS per-tenant? SLA implications for snapshot availability? We should document fallback behavior if snapshot storage is slow (i.e., prioritise API response and queue snapshot ingestion async).

elaine_pm: Good call — add requirement: async ingestion with best-effort retry and a per-snapshot ingestion status field; do not block customer responses.

sam_research: Risks & mitigations: PII leakage risk -> encrypt at rest with tenant KMS; operational complexity -> start with managed KMS and evolve to customer-managed keys; cost explosion -> sampling defaults + storage tiering.

jordan_eng: Dev tasks (rough): design schema + migrations, snapshot writer service (async), revocation service + audit log, console UI for opt-in + retention, API surface, e2e tests, perf bench.

ops-bot: Reminder: Please add security review and threat model to RFC before design review.

elaine_pm: Next steps: I'll draft the PRD with the above acceptance criteria and a short rollout plan. Ping if you want to be co-owner on the RFC (esp. @olivia_legal and @mike_sre).
